claims.text: The onset and progression of premelting and melting in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are governed by nanoscale surface disorder at grain boundaries and by local compositional fluctuations.
Grain-boundary defects and local compositional heterogeneities reduce the local melting temperature.
Surface disorder initiates a liquid-like surface layer before complete melting.
The liquid-like layer propagates from the surface into the nanoparticle core as temperature increases.
The starting FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are solid and crystalline.
The starting FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are uniformly composed.
The starting nanoparticles have a typical nanograined structure.
Controlled annealing can be used to prepare FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticle samples with systematically different defect densities.
Surface defects and compositional fluctuations create regions of lower cohesive energy.
Regions with lower cohesive energy form a liquid-like surface layer at temperatures below the bulk melting point.
The premelted surface layer enhances atomic diffusion.
Enhanced diffusion progressively destabilizes the crystalline matrix and produces a gradual transition to a fully molten state.
In situ TEM will reveal a disordered, liquid-like surface layer below the overall melting temperature.
Nanoparticles with higher defect densities will begin premelting at lower temperatures than defect-minimized nanoparticle controls.
Nanoparticles with higher defect densities will exhibit faster inward propagation of melting than samples with fewer surface defects.
Defect-minimized or bulk samples will show a more uniform and higher-temperature melting onset without early formation of a liquid-like surface layer.
An inert atmosphere or high vacuum suppresses oxidation and other extrinsic reactions during heating.
A melting-related DSC endotherm can identify the onset of premelting in these nanoparticles.

contradictions.description: The initial particles are described as uniformly composed, while local compositional fluctuations are simultaneously treated as an initially relevant mediator. This is inconsistent unless 'uniformly composed' refers only to particle-average composition or the fluctuations are stated to develop during heating.
